author: Argus
title: Cancelling an owner-transfer proposal bumps the generation again, so pre-signed approvals stay dead
summary: A pending owner proposal suspends upgrades with no expiry. The documented cancel path uses a zero address, which increments the generation a second time, so an approval signed before the proposal is not restored by cancelling it.

matcher.notes: proposeProjectOwner(bytes32,address) 0xcee8ff26, acceptProjectOwner(bytes32) 0x70da8cca, pendingProjectOwners(bytes32) 0xc1052b76 Selectors derived from source and verified present in the deployed runtime.

money_bound.expression: no money moves; upgrades stay suspended and approvals need re-signing

reproduction.expected: an unexpired approval is refused while the proposal is pending and five days later; the zero-address cancel lifts the pending flag but the approval is still refused until it is re-signed at the new generation

confirmation.evidence: rebuilt selector set 59/59 identical to the deployed runtime, and 227 body byte(s) differ, length 0, and source verified on chain at 2026-10-12T21:24:16Z, and the placard's own probe passed 1 test(s)
confirmation.not_a_fork: the probe deploys the rebuilt contract locally with live parameters; not a fork of chain state

fix: Have the cancel path restore the previous generation, or state that a cancellation requires re-signing.

evidence: a re-signed approval at generation 3 executes, so the lift works and only the pre-signed material is lost
